narrative.overview:
The system should read as a journal's offprint: warm paper, an ink-navy serif voice, hairline rules instead of boxes, and exactly one muted teal marker telling you where the action is. The look is committed to the academic record rather than a dashboard — the interface is mostly typography and rules, and its largest ornament is a published article's own title.

Density is editorial, not dense: generous section rhythm (76–104px), a 1216px measure of content, and reading columns held at ~70 characters. Colour is restrained to four voices — ivory paper, ink navy, muted teal, brass — with brass reserved for small editorial marks and never for an action. The world is light-first by identity: the default theme is warm ivory even when the operating system prefers dark, and the dark theme is a layered charcoal-navy restatement of the same hierarchy, not a separate brand.

Depth comes from tone and hairlines, not from shadow. Cards appear only where a block genuinely needs a boundary; lists of articles are hairline rows. Decoration is refused: no gradient text, no glow, no card grids standing in for a record list.
keyCharacteristics: Warm ivory paper (#faf9f6) with a white surface for panels; dark theme layers #0e1519 → #131d22
Ink navy headings (#102a3a) in Source Serif 4 at weight 600; Source Sans 3 for everything functional
One teal action per view (#24676b); the manuscript CTA keeps its own ink navy
Hairline 1px rules at 8px panel radius and 7px control radius
76–104px section rhythm, articles as rows, charts demoted behind disclosure

rules.name: The One Teal Rule
rules.body: Exactly one teal action is visible per viewport. A second teal button on the same screen is a hierarchy bug, not a style choice.

rules.name: The Brass Is Never A Button Rule
rules.body: Brass marks things; it never invites a click. No brass button, no brass link.

rules.name: The Band Is Navy Rule
rules.body: The submission band and the footer are the only full-bleed navy surfaces in the light theme, carrying their own text pair at 7.08:1. Never derive them from --heading, which flips to near-white in dark mode.

rules.name: The Heading Owns Its Weight Rule
rules.body: Headings inherit 600 and their colour from the base layer. Never add font-bold or a colour utility to an h1–h3, and never bake a colour into a display-* utility.

rules.name: The One Keyword Rule
rules.body: At most one eyebrow above a page heading; never one above every section heading. It names the page's category, not a decoration.

rules.name: The 70-Character Rule
rules.body:
Prose carries .measure (70ch). It applies to the element that bears it — not just

— which is what keeps definitions and list values from running to 118 characters.

rules.name: The Rule Before The Card Rule
rules.body: A list is hairline rows, not a card grid. Card appears only where a block genuinely needs a boundary. Nested cards are always wrong.

rules.name: The No Glow Rule
rules.body: No coloured halos, no zero-offset shadows, no gradient text. Emphasis comes from weight, size or a rule.

dos: Do use semantic tokens (bg-surface, text-muted-foreground, border-border-strong) and never a raw hex or gray-* utility.
Do reproduce the journal's published copy verbatim, and omit a section entirely when the journal has no published text for it.
Do keep the primary teal to one instance per viewport, and give the manuscript CTA the navy variant.
Do draw separators with a 4px dot element, not a · character.
Do keep body and metadata contrast at AA or better, including 13px metadata in --subtle-foreground.
Do hold prose at .measure (70ch) and let the reading size be 17px/1.8.
Do keep every control in a toolbar the same height, and every interactive target at least 24×24px.
donts: Don't add font-bold or a colour utility to an h1–h3, and don't bake colour into a display-* utility.
Don't invent scope, metrics, dates, featured status or author claims to fill a layout.
Don't put a brass-coloured button or link anywhere; brass is a mark, never an action.
Don't wrap article lists in cards, and never nest cards inside cards.
Don't use a gradient as decoration, gradient text, a coloured halo, or a zero-offset shadow.
Don't add a second eyebrow above section headings; one keyword per page heading only.
Don't let a <dd> or <li> lose its measure — a full-width definition line runs to 118 characters.
